log.why: Knocking out {lacZ, katG} splits the prior nearly in half (0.460 vs 0.540), maximizing expected information gain.
Treating at 3 µM bisects the prior probability mass (0.593 vs 0.407) to maximize information gain on Ticket 2 while Ticket 1 incubates.
E1 directly tests katG to resolve the nearly 50-50 split between katG and lacZ.
Treating at 10 uM splits the remaining probability mass evenly (0.51 vs 0.49) while Ticket 1 awaits E1.
Testing {fliC, gyrA} splits Ticket 3's prior mass nearly in half (0.544) and isolates the top two candidates while incubators are free.
Confirming lacZ (0.751 posterior) directly with E0 avoids retraction risk while using a free incubator on our most urgent ticket.
Testing fliC cleanly separates the two remaining candidates fliC (0.363) and gyrA (0.567) while starting incubation before publishing Ticket 1.
Start E11 on Ticket 4 to bisect its prior (0.506 vs 0.494) so it incubates while we immediately publish Ticket 1.
LacZ has a 0.971 posterior after three confirming knockouts, and only 4 seconds remain before expiration.
With 10s left, no plate can finish; negative E3 and positive E4 support 10 µM (0.656), beating expiration.
Test leading candidate recA (0.660) on Ticket 4 so it incubates while we publish Ticket 3's strong gyrA lead (0.839).
gyrA has strong posterior support (0.839) and only 16s remain, leaving no time to run another plate before expiration.
Test the leading candidate ftsZ directly while leaving enough time to test trpE and publish before expiration.
With 19s left on Ticket 4, we must start E2 (trpE) now to have time to read and publish if E4 (ftsZ) is negative.
Ticket 4 will expire during writing; E4 splits Ticket 5's prior nearly 50/50 at 10 µM for maximum information.
With 18s left in the round, running E5 in parallel with E4 isolates 30 µM and maximizes accuracy before publishing.
